account: Today I have been keeping my appointments: morning office business, the ten o'clock market walk, lunch at home, and now the one o'clock town accounts. Market conversations have yielded little news. Several townsfolk reported that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery; that sounds consistent with baking supplies, and I have no evidence that it means anything unusual. The builder was at the market, but I have heard no specific business from them. The unresolved matter is my three o'clock tea: my appointment book lists a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank without naming the host or exact cottage. The secretary took the appointment book and said they would investigate the east-bank cottages and report back. They are now near the town hall holding a writable book. I have just asked for accounts to review and whether the tea arrangements are confirmed; I have not yet heard an answer. I do not know whether the vague tea entry is anything more than an incomplete appointment.
